description: The TIMES-Ireland Model (TIM) is a whole-energy-system optimisation model of Ireland, built on the TIMES framework, that finds the lowest-cost way to restructure electricity, transport, industry, residential and commercial energy and new fuels such as hydrogen and bioenergy to meet emission targets. It is developed by the MaREI Energy Policy and Modelling Group at University College Cork as the successor to the Irish TIMES Model used since 2010, and is described in a 2022 Geoscientific Model Development paper; tagged releases reach v1.2.0, with commits into May 2026. Its first scenarios informed the Climate Change Advisory Council's carbon budget recommendations, and scenario results are on Zenodo with a web viewer. Studies built on it include a district heating study whose inputs and results are archived on Zenodo. Coverage is Ireland. The model files are accessible on GitHub at no cost under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: running it needs the TIMES modelling framework, and the licence forbids commercial use. Simulation uses are national decarbonisation pathways, sector coupling and district heating and hydrogen planning. Related records: data-cso-ireland-networked-gas-consumption gives Irish gas use statistics.
